title: Periodic Habits
subject: chemistry
author: Clueberry Desk
introduction: Nine elements you have already met today.

entries.clue: Roughly a fifth of the air
entries.explanation: Dry air is about 21 per cent by volume.
Table salt is sodium chloride, one atom of each.

entries.clue: Heavy metal once used for pipes

factCards.text: Helium was spotted in the spectrum of sunlight in 1868, years before anyone found it on Earth — which is why it is named after Helios.
factCards.sourceTitle: Royal Society of Chemistry — Periodic Table: Helium

factCards.text: Table salt is sodium chloride: a lattice with one sodium ion for every chloride ion.
factCards.sourceTitle: Royal Society of Chemistry — Periodic Table: Sodium

factCards.text: A tube of pure neon glows orange-red. The blues, greens and whites of a sign come from other gases or from phosphor coatings inside the glass.
factCards.sourceTitle: Royal Society of Chemistry — Periodic Table: Neon
